issues: Minor (low): the version regex ^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$ accepts leading zeros (verified: '01.0.0' was ACCEPTED, exit 0), so a tag like v01.0.0 could be published. This matches the regex the goal explicitly prescribed, so it is not an acceptance-criteria deviation; suggested hardening is (0|[1-9][0-9]*)\. for each numeric identifier.

Minor (low, cosmetic): in README.md the new sentence 'You can pin the plugin image to robkaandorp/drone-portainer:v1.0.0 ...' sits between '...deploy a compose file to portainer. For example:' and its YAML example block, so the 'For example:' sentence reads as introducing the pinning sentence. The goal only required the sentence be added.

Environment note (not a code defect): git in this container could not resolve the 40-char merge-base SHA 210195919b242e976cf6844c65467d1ccb69 (0/30 attempts) even though the object is present in the pack index, 'git fsck --full --strict' passes, 'git rev-list --all' lists it, and the 39-char and 7-char short forms resolve fine. Verified the repository is intact; used the equivalent short SHA 2101959 for diff-based checks.

Test-harness note (not a code defect): 'gh release create' has no --dry-run flag, so one probe of the release command actually created a real release and tag v0.0.0-test on the remote. This was detected and immediately cleaned up (gh release delete + DELETE git/refs/tags); re-verified via the API that the remote has zero releases and zero tags, and the guard still passes for v1.0.0.
